segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for October 19th, 2026.
Today we cover funding for construction bots, advanced autonomous driving partnerships, and some surprisingly mundane robot feats.
Tune in for the latest.
From Robotics & Automation News, Origin raises twenty million dollars to scale general-purpose construction robots.
This funding is designated for the deployment of its flagship robot, the OG-1, and the expansion of its fleet across pilot programs in the United States and Europe.
The OG-1 autonomously executes wall-finishing tasks by employing a Construction Action Model trained on actual job site data.
The company intends to extend the robot's functionality beyond wall finishing to encompass other interior trades, aiming to automate interior construction processes.
Origin projects the deployment of one hundred fifty robots by the close of two thousand twenty-seven, with the objective of enhancing both construction speed and quality through this automation.
This development signals continued investment in applying advanced robotics to complex physical labor within the construction sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Mercedes-Benz and Nvidia deepen partnership on automated driving.
This report details the extension of the strategic collaboration to advance automated driving systems through the combination of engineering expertise and advanced computing technologies.
The collaboration involves integrating Mercedes-Benz's engineering knowledge and MB.OS with Nvidia's artificial intelligence and accelerated computing technologies.
Specific development focuses on integrating MB.OS with Nvidia Hyperion for in-vehicle computing and sensor architecture.
Nvidia's Alpamayo Stack provides full-stack driving software and Nvidia Halos are utilized to enhance safety for advanced driver assistance.
Further scope includes vehicle engineering simulation and the digital production ecosystem.
This collaboration signifies a convergence of automotive engineering and advanced AI computing in the development of autonomous systems.
Future developments in vehicle autonomy will reflect this integrated technological approach.

From Humanoid.guide, Robostrategy CEO Andrew Kang stated that a Taku robot was deployed at Din Tai Fung in New York to fold napkins, demonstrating the capability of robotic systems in hospitality environments.
This development highlights the application of physical AI in routine service tasks within commercial settings.
Andrew Kang indicated that automating repetitive textile tasks in hospitality allows employees to concentrate on more skilled work.
The current focus for robot deployments involves specialized tasks such as napkin folding, laundry folding, and data center operations.
The development strategy centers on building physical AI around constrained tasks to accumulate necessary experience before achieving broader capabilities.
Kang anticipates that these specialized models will eventually generalize to a wider range of human activities.
This trend signals a shift toward embedding physical AI into daily workflows for practical skill acquisition.
From Humanoid.guide, "Agility targets nine minute charging for Digit 5 humanoid".

This report details Agility Robotics' plan to equip the Digit 5 humanoid with Nyobolt batteries, achieving approximately ninety minutes of work time from only nine minutes of charging, resulting in a ten to one ratio of working time to charging time.
The methodology involves the integration of Nyobolt battery technology into the Digit 5 platform.
This advancement significantly improves operational efficiency compared to the previous Digit 4 model.

The Nyobolt batteries are characterized as lightweight and engineered to endure multiple charging cycles, with the aim of allowing the robot to operate for over twenty hours daily, which is projected to enhance business economics.
The company is also investigating battery swapping as a future development for subsequent humanoid models.
This development suggests a significant step toward improving the operational viability and economic feasibility of humanoid robotics.

From Robotics & Automation News, The Robot Group has opened UK enquiries for X-Humanoid robots, seeking projects involving the company's TianGong and Tianyi humanoid robots for applications across manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, and infrastructure.
The distributor will assist prospective customers in defining requirements and assessing suitable robot platforms.
X-Humanoid robots, including the TianGong Ultra, have received international attention for their demonstrated capabilities.
Interested UK organizations can engage with The Robot Group to discuss specific applications and explore these robotic solutions.
This initiative facilitates the introduction of advanced humanoid robotics into various industrial sectors within the United Kingdom.
The growing market for advanced automation suggests increasing integration of humanoid systems into commercial operations moving forward.
From Robotics & Automation News, "QCraft partners with HERE Technologies to expand autonomous driving in Europe".

This report details a memorandum of understanding established between QCraft and HERE Technologies to integrate HERE's map data with QCraft's navigation-assisted driving technology to accelerate the local validation and rollout of intelligent driving solutions across Europe and other international markets.

The collaboration involves combining QCraft's expertise in autonomy with HERE's location intelligence, recognizing the necessity of accurate, localized map data for navigation systems which vary considerably across European nations.

This integration is designed to foster safer and more reliable driving experiences by leveraging precise location information alongside autonomous capabilities, supporting QCraft's approach of delivering global technology with local service.
This development signals a strategic step toward standardizing and enhancing the deployment of autonomous driving technologies through geographically specific data integration.
From Humanoid.guide, China bets on robotic hands to strengthen humanoid industry.
This report details China's investment in dexterous robotic hands as a crucial element for its humanoid manufacturing goals.
The complexity of hand manipulation is a major technical obstacle in creating functional humanoids due to the difficulty in coordinating grasping and multiple movements.
Government subsidies and a robust domestic supply chain are providing advantages for this industry push.
Companies such as Linkerbot are currently developing this technology for various applications across different sectors.
This development also serves to address domestic labor needs by utilizing robots to fill workforce gaps.
This focus indicates a strategic move toward advanced robotics integration within the manufacturing sector.
Further developments in this area will shape the trajectory of humanoid technology and automation deployment.
From Robohub, "Powered by muscle cells, a paper-thin robot swims through watery maze".
This report details the development of a soft robot utilizing muscle cells to navigate a watery maze by flapping fins in response to light exposure.
MIT engineers achieved this by engineering muscle cells to twitch when exposed to light, allowing flashing light to control the robot's direction and speed through the water.
The research involved optimizing the underlying gel skeleton and muscle alignment to maximize the force generated by these muscle movements.
This work represents a significant advancement toward creating thin, efficient, and self-healing biohybrid robots.
This development signals progress in biomimetic robotics and the creation of advanced soft material systems.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Is OTA for ROS 2 robots a solved problem?".

This segment addresses the challenges in establishing a dedicated solution for Over-The-Air updates within the ROS 2 ecosystem, revealing that implementing functional self-updating mechanisms presents significant complexities beyond simple container distribution.
An author conducted a personal project using a Raspberry Pi to develop an updater that retrieved container images from GitHub and incorporated a rollback feature.

The author determined that achieving a fully functional updater introduced difficulties related to self-updating mechanisms, noting that while approaches like A/B updates are available, each involves specific operational trade-offs.
Input from production robot users regarding existing tools such as Mender or balena for ROS 2 OTA is being sought.
The ongoing investigation into robust update methodologies is necessary for future robotic deployment scalability.
From The Robot Report, "How to choose a BLDC motor for robotic arms and mobile robots"
details the necessary considerations for selecting Brushless DC motors in robotic systems, emphasizing that mechanical system and load profile take precedence over controller specifications.
The selection process necessitates calculations involving torque, speed, and power, factoring in gear ratios and efficiency prior to controller selection.
Control methods such as Field-Oriented Control provide advantages for smooth motion, and feedback selection is determined by the required position accuracy and mechanical transmission.
The integration of controller and feedback must account for system-level concerns including thermal limits, communication protocols, and safety architecture.
A structured workflow involving load definition, motion profiling, and system validation is crucial for optimal motor selection.
This methodology establishes a framework for engineering reliable and efficient robotic hardware components.
And that's all the circuits we have time for today!
Origin is building the future, one robot at a time.
Thanks for tuning into your daily dose of robotics.
Until tomorrow, keep those gears turning!
